verses.1: And Shimehon went to Azota. There he saw a beautiful woman, and he went up to her.
verses.2: To the Israelites, it was said, “The sun has risen. They stood at the gates of the city all night long, waiting until morning to kill him.”
verses.3: And Shimehon lay down until half the night. Then he got up at midnight, and he held onto the doors of the city gates. He led them away with his troops. He put a veil over their faces, and then he went up to the top of the mountain that was located in front of Haboron.
verses.4: And after that, he loved a woman named Delila.
verses.5: And the officials of Phileas came to her and said, “Give him up! Look at his great power and what he can do. We forbid him from resisting him. We will give you one thousand and one hundred pieces of silver.”
verses.6: And Delilah said to Shemashon, “Please tell me what your power is, and what it is that you forbid others from doing.”
verses.7: And Shemoshon said to her, “If I am forbidden to eat seven hard foods that have not been crushed, and if I become sick, then I will be like one of those people.”
verses.8: And the priests of Philistia brought seven rotten pieces of wood to her. These pieces of wood had not been burned, and they were therefore forbidden to be used.
verses.9: And the angel sat down beside her in the room. She said to him, “Philistim, they have set up a lamp for you.” Then he cut off the ropes, just as Phutilah cut off the ropes when he burned the girl. But we don’t know what his strength was.
verses.10: And Delilah said to Shemashon, “Look, you have been deceived by me. Now, tell me, please, what is it that is forbidden?”
verses.11: And he said to her, “If they forbid me from doing these new tasks that haven’t been done yet, then I will become like any other person.”
verses.12: And Delilah took some new bracelets and put them on him. Then she said to him, “Philistine, the sun will rise over you, and the moon will stand in its place. It will be destroyed by its own seeds.”
verses.13: And Delilah said to Shmashon, “Until now, you have been in me. You spoke to me like a liar. You told me what is forbidden.” He replied, “If you can arrange the seven changes of the head with the mask…”
verses.14: And it was inserted into the yatad. Then she said to him, “Philistine, Shoshon has come after you.” He got up from his seat and carried away the yatad and the mask.
verses.15: And she said to him, “How can you say that you love me? Your heart does not belong to me. You’ve been with me three times, yet you never told me how great your strength is.”
verses.16: And it happened that, because she constantly spoke to him in those words, his spirit became weak and he was on the verge of death.
verses.17: And he poured out all his heart to her. He said to her, “Do not be afraid. I am a servant of God. From my mother’s womb, I have been like any other man. If I fall and become weak, then I will be just like all people.”
verses.18: And Delilah saw that he had told her everything in his heart. So she sent for the men of Samson and said, “Come here this time, because he has told me everything in his heart.” And the men of Samson came to her, carrying gold coins in their hands.
verses.19: She changed her clothes, called out to the man, and removed seven of his bracelets. Then she began to question him. He then took away the power from him.
verses.20: And the Philistines said to him, “Shamshon!” He then left his place and went away. But he didn’t know that Jehovah had rejected him.
verses.21: And the Philistines seized him, cut out his eyes, and took him away to Azota. They put him in a prison, and he became a prisoner in the house of those who imprisoned people.
verses.22: And his forehead began to bleed, just as it was cut open.
verses.23: And the people of Sodom gathered together to offer a great sacrifice to their gods, for their joy. They said, “Our God has given us the sun in our hands!”
verses.24: And the people saw him, and they praised their gods. They said, “Our God has given us our enemies into our hands; he has also caused our land to be destroyed, and he has increased our suffering.”
verses.25: And their hearts were filled with joy. They said, “Call Shimeh here.” So they called Shimeh from among the people of Asur. He came forward and stood between them.
verses.26: And Shimshon said to the boy who held the rod in his hand, “Put it down. And let the idols be removed from there.”
verses.27: And the house was filled with men and women. All the people of Philistia were there. On the roof, there were three thousand men and women who stared at the sun.
verses.28: And Shemson called out to Jehovah, and said, “Lord Jehovah, please remember me. Strengthen me, for this time is a time of vengeance. I will avenge one of my people from the hands of the Philistines.”
verses.29: And Shimon set up the two pillars on which the house was built. He placed one of them on his right hand, and the other on his left.
verses.30: And Shemoshan said, “My soul shall rest with the Philistines.” He then attacked with his strength, and the house collapsed upon the people who were inside it. Many of those who died in that attack were more numerous than those who died during his lifetime.
verses.31: And his brothers and all the household of his father came and laid him in a tomb, between Zareah and Etam. His father had judged Israel for forty years.
